messages:
Liang: Noticed a regression on canary: prefix cache hit-rate fell from ~98% to ~84% after the recent tokenizer bump. Short-chat p50 increased ~28ms. Profiler trace: https://perf.internal/runs/2230011223
Sam: Any obvious changes in kernel selection or quantization that coincided?
Maria: Canary has tokenizer v3.3.0 (reordered tokenstream fields) + kernel-selector v1.4.1. No quant flip AFAICT. Junaid, can you pull warmup and cache telemetry?
Junaid: Warmup logs show many formerly-hot prefix keys now missing. KV evictions also up ~20%. Replay with prior tokenizer shows hit-rate returns to ~97%.
Liang: I think tokenstream reordering changes how we serialize tool/function metadata when building cache keys. The model input is semantically identical but the raw bytes differ -> new cache key. Meanwhile kernel-selector picked the int8 short-path expecting high cache locality; with misses, batching heuristics over-commit and latency spikes.
Eli: Can you paste an example of the serialized diff (simplified)?
Liang: Sure:
```
OLD_SERIAL: {"sys":"assistant","tool":{"calls":[{"name":"search","q":"x"}],"env":"prod"}}
NEW_SERIAL: {"sys":"assistant","tool":{"env":"prod","calls":[{"name":"search","q":"x"}]}}
```
Liang: Same data, different ordering. Our cache key = sha1(json.dumps(tool_meta)) today, so ordering matters.
Sam: We debated canonicalization before but never landed it in the hot path. Options: add deterministic canonicalizer for tool_meta, or include tokenizer version + serializer-hash in the key to isolate cross-version drift.
Maria: Short-term mitigation: roll the tokenizer back on the canary and gate any kernel-selector changes behind cache-hit deltas. Medium-term: normalizing encoder/serializer output before hashing.
Junaid: Quick patch I ran locally: lightweight canonicalizer that sorts object keys and normalizes arrays of known structures (sort by 'name' for call lists). Replay with this canonicalizer restored hit-rate to 95% in our synthetic workload. Overhead: ~0.6ms per request for the key path.
Sam: 0.6ms is non-trivial but acceptable if behind a feature flag and A/B'd. Suggest route 10% traffic to canonicalizer first. Monitor CPU and end-to-end p50.
Liang: Proposed key change (short-term): cache_key = sha1(tokenizer_version + "|" + canonicalize(tool_meta)). That prevents cross-version collisions and fixes intra-version ordering when canonicalize enabled.
Eli: Also need to update the batching heuristic: it assumes a hit-rate baseline when estimating token cost. If hit-rate drops, heuristic should prefer latency-first (smaller batches) rather than cost-first. Add a test that simulates hit-rates 60-90% to validate.
Junaid: I'll add a regression in runtime-tests that replays traffic with configurable hit-rate and asserts batching selection falls back correctly.
Maria: I'll open a rollback for tokenizer on canary and add a perf-gate: any canary that shows cache-hit delta > 5 percentage points blocks kernel-selector or quant changes. Ops-bot, schedule rollback window.
ops-bot: Rollback of tokenizer v3.3.0 to v3.2.0 scheduled for 16:05 UTC; health-check at +5m.
Liang: Action items:
- liang: PR for key change + feature flag for canonicalize (A/B 10%)
- junaid: batching heuristic regression + add KV eviction monitor in warmup metrics
- maria: canary rollback + perf-gate rule for kernel flips
- sam: instrument kernel-selector to emit cache-hit signals to the heuristic
Sam: Also consider shipping a small offline tool to diff keys across serializer versions so infra can scan canaries before rollout. Simple map of sha1s per prefix will do.
Liang: I'll drop a small cache-diff tool under infra/tools/cache-diff and link it in the PR. I'll post PR links and a replay summary in this thread once ready.
Maria: Good work catching this. Rolling back and gating should prevent customer exposure.
Liang: Thanks — will follow up with numbers from the 10% A/B once it's live.
